finding: A client's reconnect (session renew) to slow follower F1 is delayed on the network; the client times out, re-establishes the session on F2, and works there. The late ConnectRequest then reaches F1, F1 sends REVALIDATE to the leader, and the leader sets the session owner to F1's LearnerHandler. Every later request from the client over its only live connection (F2) is then rejected with SessionMovedException at SessionTrackerImpl.java:246, and the connection stays open (3/3 setData failures).
same_root_cause: Yes, same defect. The stale revalidation path is LearnerHandler.java:403-409 (touch, then an unconditional leader.zk.setOwner(id, this)), which makes the owner diverge from the client's real server. PrepRequestProcessor.pRequest:308 -> SessionTrackerImpl.checkSession:244-246 then throws SessionMovedException, and the buggy FinalRequestProcessor (catch KeeperException at :330) returns it to the client as an ordinary error code without closing the connection, so the error is permanent. The fix's FinalRequestProcessor hunk (catch SessionMovedException -> cnxn.sendCloseSession()) targets exactly this sequence; its own comment describes it ('client on slow follower starts to renew session, fails before this completes, then tries the fast follower ... the initial renew is then successfully fwd/processed by the leader ... client and leader disagree').
realistic: Yes. It uses a real 3-server QuorumPeer ensemble and the real client. The only intervention is a TCP proxy in front of F1 that holds the client's bytes until the client has timed out and moved to F2, then delivers them: a network delay. The leader's SessionTrackerImpl subclass calls super and only records the exception. Shuffling the server list until F1 is tried first is ordinary client behaviour. No reflection, no fabricated arguments, no protocol shortcut.
fixed_version: This is a handle-not-prevent fix, so the check still fires once at SessionTrackerImpl.java:246 on the fixed tree. But the server now closes the client's F2 connection (log: 'Closed socket connection ... 11224', client 'attempting reconnect'), and the first setData gets ConnectionLossException instead of SessionMovedException. Only one server-side rejection is logged, against 3 on the buggy tree. So the permanent SESSIONMOVED consequence is gone, as the fix intends.
reason: The agent reproduced the exact interleaving in the ZOOKEEPER-710 fix comment: a stale renew from a slow follower is processed by the leader after the client has moved, and the session owner diverges. On the buggy code the client's live connection gets SessionMovedException on every request without being torn down, which is the JIRA's consequence. The trigger is a realistic network delay, and the fixed version turns the permanent error into a connection loss the client recovers from.
